identity.spin_note: Four I=1/2 protons give a spin product 2^4=16. Divide spectroscopic Q by 16 to compare with nuclear-spin-free thermochemistry in the high-temperature equilibrium convention. Td state weights 5,5,2,3,3 are already included. Do not additionally divide by rotational symmetry 12 or confuse the HITRAN state-independent gi=1 with the complete spin product. No isotope-resolved equilibrium is modeled.

printed_janaf.evaluation: March 1961; current table converted to 1 bar
printed_janaf.uncertainty_definition: Not separately recovered; do not interpret as 95% limits or propagate independently.
thermal_ancestry: Stevenson and Ibers (1960): bond distance and force constants
printed_janaf.energy_ancestry: Rossini (1931) combustion, recomputed with then-accepted formation enthalpies of water and CO2.

atct.uncertainty_definition: Estimated 95% confidence limits; correlated network, not propagated as independent errors.
atct.independence_note: ATcT combines calorimetry, equilibrium and theory. Thermal functions enter third-law reductions; the energy evaluation does not independently validate the full high-temperature thermal curve.

wenger2008.method: Fitted lower polyads plus statistical rotational and Morse extrapolation of high polyads toward dissociation
wenger2008.uncertainty_note: At 300 and 1000 K the reported value is less than 0.1%, represented here as an upper bound. These are model-based estimates, not specified confidence intervals. Nikitin (2015) later questions the high-energy statistical approximation; retain this as a historical diagnostic, not a preferred benchmark.

mm2024.note: Calculated energies are replaced by MARVEL energies where available. The downloaded file extends to 5000 K, but the published completeness estimate is 2000 K. No all-state caloric validation to 4000 K is established.

followups: Reconcile CH4 TIPS2021 and TIPS2025 arrays against versioned original datasets and generators; investigate truncation, models and publication/file differences without assuming their cause.
Resolve the residual between the 2017 corrected printed fit and 2015 Tables 3/5, using original numerical data or author clarification; the full papers and corrected coefficients are now inspected.
Obtain bound-state and near-dissociation coverage with first and second energy moments through 4000 K, using common isotope and spin conventions.
Then choose a continuous G/H/S/Cp model and evaluate a finite equilibrium substitution.
decision: Retain the existing JANAF molecular thermal functions, NASA atomic thermal functions and balanced ATcT energy operationally. The inspected Nikitin 2015/2017 treatment adds qualified evidence through 3000 K but does not resolve 4000 K coverage, caloric convergence, or its printed-fit/table residual. Neither raw NASA nor a wholesale MM/TIPS/Nikitin replacement is justified over 1500-4000 K. Physical accuracy remains unknown.

nikitin2015_2017.inspection: Full 2015 paper (pp. 53-63) and one-page 2017 correction inspected from user-supplied PDFs; Tables 3 and 5 and corrected Table 4 checked visually.
nikitin2015_2017.method: High-order contact transformations from the NRT potential, symmetry-block ratios and high-P/high-J extrapolations, compared with expanded-basis variational calculations using the same potential.
nikitin2015_2017.logarithm_convention: Base 10 reproduces the scale of published Q values; natural logarithms do not. Shared interval endpoints use the higher-temperature interval in the audit.
nikitin2015_2017.internal_consistency_note: The printed 1500 K Table 3 total (40424.32) differs from Table 5 (40382) by 0.1048%. Neither value is silently substituted for the other. The corrected printed fit exceeds Table 3 totals by 0.61-0.80%, larger than the approximately 0.1% interpolation accuracy stated in Section 4.3. The cause is unresolved; distinguish these reproducible representation residuals from physical accuracy.
nikitin2015_2017.uncertainty_definition: Author model estimates, not specified confidence intervals. Above 2000 K the authors explicitly do not quantify reliable error bars, especially because of P,J extrapolation; a 3000 K tabulation does not establish completeness or accuracy at 4000 K.
convergence_notes: Table 1 directly diagonalizes selected symmetry/P/J blocks; asymptotic symmetry ratios and extrapolations fill the remaining contributions. Table 3 is not a fully direct, converged state sum.
Section 6 reports levels extended to about 25000 cm-1 and J up to 80 for P=10; Table 3 includes extrapolated contributions through P=20.
Low-J variational basis expansion approaches CT contributions to about 1%; this is a shared-potential numerical comparison, not independent experimental validation of the high-energy tail.

Section 5 contains apparent exponent slips for the 2500 K variational/CT estimates; use the explicitly printed Table 3/5 totals and preserve the reported 6.5% comparison as an author statement, without repairing raw text.
No converged first/second energy moments or whole-domain G/H/S/Cp model through 4000 K is supplied.
nikitin2015_2017.correction_scope: The 2017 notice adds digits to fitted Table 4 and says the other tables, figures and conclusions are unchanged; no new physical state calculation is reported.
nikitin2015_2017.adoption: Useful additional Q evidence through 3000 K, with qualified accuracy near 2000 K. Do not adopt the polynomial as a validated thermal model through 4000 K or extrapolate it beyond 3000 K.
